# Incident Report: 2021-09-10 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.9.10.102** | Top talker in `conv,ip`; source of all infection-related traffic |
| MAC | **00:4f:49:b1:e8:c3** | ARP: `10.9.10.102 → 00:4f:49:b1:e8:c3` (consistent across all ARP replies) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-KKITB6Q** | NBNS name registration from 10.9.10.102 (`DESKTOP-KKITB6Q<00>`, `<20>`); DHCP option 12 hostname `DESKTOP-KKITB6Q` tied to MAC `00:4f:49:b1:e8:c3` |
| AD domain | `angrypoutine.com` (NetBIOS `ANGRYPOUTINE`, DC at 10.9.10.9 `ANGRYPOUTINE-DC`) | NBNS/DNS records |
| Logged-in user | **hobart.gunnarsson** | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS traffic between 10.9.10.102 and DC 10.9.10.9 |

## Malware Family

**IcedID (aka Bokbot)** — attribution is **behavioral**, not signature-confirmed. No IDS/Suricata alert files were present in the evidence directory, so this is based on traffic pattern analysis, not a rule hit:

1. Infection stager: a GET request from the victim to a compromised legitimate web server, downloading an encrypted/packed DLL disguised with a generic `Content-Disposition` filename.
2. Post-infection: sustained, low-volume, evenly-spaced TLS "check-in" sessions to a hosting-provider IP, all presenting an **identical self-signed certificate** with formulaic, clearly fabricated identity fields (fake country/city/org strings, not from any real CA).

This gate→encrypted-payload→self-signed-cert-beacon chain matches IcedID's well-documented delivery and C2 pattern from this period. Absent a hash match against a known reference database (not attempted — no internet access permitted for this analysis), it cannot be signature-confirmed.

## Timeline (relative to capture start, 2021-09-11 03:15:07 +0400)

- **t+139s** — 10.9.10.102 resolves `simpsonsavingss.com` → 194.62.42.206
- **t+140s** — 10.9.10.102 issues `GET /bmdff/BhoHsCtZ/MLdmpfjaX/5uFG3Dz7yt/date1?BNLv65=pAAS` to `simpsonsavingss.com`; server returns a 284,816-byte PE32+ x86-64 DLL with `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="date6"`
- **t+144s onward** — first TLS session to 167.172.37.9:443 (single ~303 KB session, 4.5s), presenting the self-signed `londonareloeli.uk` certificate
- **t+148s through t+4512s** (≈73 minutes, spanning nearly the entire capture) — repeated short TLS sessions (5–9 KB each, roughly every 100–460 seconds) from 10.9.10.102 to **94.158.245.52:443**, every one presenting the same self-signed certificate — classic C2 beaconing cadence

## Indicators of Compromise

### C2 endpoints
| IOC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| `94.158.245.52:443` | 15 distinct TCP sessions over ~73 min, uniform small payload sizes (5–9 KB), all TLS with the `londonareloeli.uk` self-signed cert — beaconing pattern |
| `167.172.37.9:443` | Single 303 KB TLS session at t+144s, same self-signed cert as above — likely second-stage module/config pull |

### Malicious domain
| IOC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| `simpsonsavingss.com` | DNS query at t+139s resolving to 194.62.42.206; HTTP `Host:` header on the payload-download GET request |

### Malicious URL
| IOC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| `http://simpsonsavingss.com/bmdff/BhoHsCtZ/MLdmpfjaX/5uFG3Dz7yt/date1?BNLv65=pAAS` | Frame 1189, TCP stream 50; server response headers: `Server: Apache/2.4.6 (CentOS) OpenSSL/1.0.2k-fips PHP/7.2.34` (a compromised legitimate web server used as a "gate"), `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="date6"`, `Content-Length: 284816` |

### Dropped/transferred file
| IOC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| File name (server-supplied): `date6` | HTTP response `Content-Disposition` header, TCP stream 50 |
| SHA256: `eed363fc4af7a9070d69340592dcab7c78db4f90710357de29e3b624aa957cf8` | Computed from the object carved out of TCP stream 50 (matches `Content-Length: 284816`); file type confirmed as `PE32+ executable (DLL) (GUI) x86-64, for MS Windows` |

### Self-signed C2 certificate (fingerprint for detection, not a standalone IOC type but ties both C2 IPs together)
- CN=`londonareloeli.uk`, OU=`UK System`, O=`LL EST`, L=`London`, ST=`London`, C=`UK`; issuer == subject (self-signed). Observed identically on both 94.158.245.52 and 167.172.37.9.

## Benign Context (ruled out, not IOCs)
- All `*.windowsupdate.com`, `*.msftncsi.com`, `*.microsoft.com`, `*.msedge.net`, `*.msn.com`, `login.live.com`, `officeapps.live.com`, `s-microsoft.com` (Windows Store images), `update.googleapis.com`, `gameplayapi.intel.com`, `cdn.onenote.net` — standard Windows/Microsoft telemetry, Windows Update (including a legitimate Defender `am_delta_patch` definition update), and Store traffic.
- `myexternalip.com` (34.117.59.81) — single TLS session, no correlating suspicious follow-up traffic; likely a benign network-connectivity check tool, insufficient evidence to call malicious.
- Internal AD/domain traffic: Kerberos, LDAP/CLDAP, DCE-RPC (SAMR, LSARPC, DRSUAPI, Netlogon), SMB/SMB2 to 10.9.10.9/10.9.10.103 — normal domain-joined workstation behavior, not indicative of lateral movement in this capture.
- SSDP/mDNS/LLMNR/NBNS broadcast noise — normal LAN discovery chatter.

## Incident Summary

The Windows workstation **DESKTOP-KKITB6Q** (10.9.10.102, MAC 00:4f:49:b1:e8:c3), logged in as domain user **hobart.gunnarsson**, was infected with malware behaviorally consistent with **IcedID (Bokbot)**. At t+140s into the capture the host retrieved an encrypted PE32+ DLL payload from a compromised web server at `simpsonsavingss.com` (194.62.42.206) via a randomized-path gate URL. The host then established persistent, evenly-spaced TLS check-in traffic to `94.158.245.52:443` (and one larger session to `167.172.37.9:443`) for the remainder of the capture, both endpoints presenting an identical fabricated self-signed certificate (CN `londonareloeli.uk`), consistent with C2 beaconing.
